knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Changes to the schedule or product for a patient condition are agreed with clinical management and the infection prevention service.
The standard requires food-grade, perfume-free products wherever food is handled in a clinical or ward setting.
The standard says the cadence of cleaning and spot cleaning in shared areas might need increasing to match how likely bodily fluids are to contaminate them.

practicalCriteria: Learner identifies from a sample product label whether it is food grade and free of perfume, with the correct decision given
Learner states the approval route for a product change, with the unit manager and infection prevention named
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Assessor record of the label check
Approval route noted on the sample record
stopWorkCriteria: A product in a kitchenette is fragranced or not food grade
A patient sensitivity is recorded and no approved alternative exists
